title: E15 — 02-feedback: logging telemetry cleanup, --debug flag, save-on-exit popup
description:
Tracks the four feedback items in specs/02-feedback.md (trunk snapshot 3c2f365; current trunk 59b5018): two logging items (undocumented LODE_LOG_LEVEL; debug logs corrupting the TUI console), a new top-level --debug CLI flag to enable diagnostic instrumentation, and a UX fix so the save-on-exit confirm is a popup over the editor instead of a full blank screen.

## Design decisions (confirmed with user 2026-07-04; refined after /debate)
- Item 3 (lode-1i8.2) = TUI-ONLY file logging. Suppress console/stderr log output only while the TUI runs, keeping the file handler (and guaranteeing one is attached so Python's lastResort can't fire). Plain CLI commands (ask/add) KEEP stderr — 'lode ask' deliberately mirrors an AuthError's cause to stderr; that path is preserved. (Re-scoped from an earlier 'drop stderr globally' after debate flagged the CLI regression.)
- Item 2 (lode-1i8.3) = TOP-LEVEL 'lode --debug' flag on the root Typer callback: sets DEBUG log level + enables diagnostic instrumentation (event-loop-lag probe, etc.) for every subcommand. Accepted coupling: --debug == DEBUG log level (verbosity == feature-enablement); split later if needed.
- Item 4 (lode-1i8.4) = external Textual .tcss stylesheet (repo's first), wired via CSS_PATH and shipped via pyproject package-data.

## Sequencing
- .2 blocks .3 (shared logconfig/cli files).
- .1 blocks .3 (both edit docs/configuration.md — avoid merge collision; .3 appends to the logging section .1 creates).
- .4 is independent.

Related prior epic lode-0wj (E14) delivered the exit-safety confirm guard (lode-0wj.1 Escape, lode-0wj.8 Ctrl+Q) and the lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2) whose probe is gated on DEBUG; item 4 here refines that confirm UX.

## Success Criteria
- LODE_LOG_LEVEL (and ANTHROPIC_LOG) documented in docs/configuration.md.
- A top-level 'lode --debug' flag raises log level to DEBUG and enables diagnostic instrumentation across all subcommands.
- Running 'lode tui' writes ZERO log output to the terminal (console suppressed for the TUI session, file handler retained), so latency telemetry is collectible via the log file without corrupting the TUI; plain CLI stderr logging is unchanged.
- Pressing Escape (or Ctrl+Q) over a dirty capture buffer shows a centered popup dialog (external .tcss, shipped in the wheel) over the still-visible editor; Cancel dismisses it and returns to the editor unchanged.

title: Instrument the capture screen: reveal what runs during input (lag diagnosis spike)
description: Feedback: typing feels laggy/blocked and it's unclear what the app does behind the scenes. Add lightweight, toggleable instrumentation (timing/logging around the event loop, keystroke->render latency, and the passive related-notes worker: how often it fires, how long find_related_notes / the ONNX embedder / LanceDB take, whether passes overlap). Prime suspect: on_text_area_changed debounces a pass that runs the embedder+LanceDB via asyncio.to_thread on every idle pause. Goal is DATA, not a fix: identify what actually blocks input. Blocks the optimisation follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: REPRO PRECONDITION: reproduce the felt lag against a realistic seeded corpus (reuse the deterministic seed-corpus fixture from lode-5y8.4), NOT an empty DB — an empty/small DB makes the related-notes pass return instantly and hides the lag. Define a target keystroke->render latency (e.g. p95 threshold) so the spike has a pass/fail, not just 'notes'. MUST-ANSWER: does the passive related-notes worker actually yield the event loop? i.e. does the fastembed/ONNX embed release the GIL during inference — asyncio.to_thread only relieves input if it does; if ONNX holds the GIL the 'background' pass stalls typing anyway. Deliverable: findings on this ticket (what runs on the input path, measured cost, and the GIL/event-loop-yield verdict). No behaviour change beyond instrumentation.
notes:
Debate (lode-0wj): the prime suspect (related-notes pass) is ALREADY off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread + @work(exclusive=True) in src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py, so on paper it should not block input. The one mechanism that WOULD make it block: to_thread does not help if the offloaded C code holds the GIL — fastembed/ONNX inference may not release it. Verifying that is the load-bearing question for whether lode-0wj.3 (disable related-notes) is the right fix or a red herring.
FINDINGS (spike, git 96e2c19, tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py, opt-in LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1):

Reproduced against the REAL lode-5y8.4 seed corpus (10 notes) with the REAL
fastembed/ONNX embedder (not the eval scorer's offline hash stub) -- an empty
DB was avoided per the acceptance precondition.

PASS/FAIL TARGET: p95 event-loop tick lag < 100ms during the pass (the
standard "feels instant" interactive-response threshold), measured as how much
longer a 10ms asyncio.sleep heartbeat comes back late by -- a direct proxy for
keystroke->render latency since Textual's key handling/repaint run on the same
event loop.

MUST-ANSWER, DIRECT RESULT: YES, fastembed/ONNX DOES release the GIL during
inference, and asyncio.to_thread IS relieving input as designed.
  - find_related_notes cost against the seeded corpus: min=52-63ms
    mean=64-68ms p95=70-76ms max=70-76ms (5 realistic mid-typing drafts).
  - Event-loop lag, full find_related_notes pass (FTS5+ONNX+LanceDB) via
    asyncio.to_thread, sustained over 10 repeated passes: idle baseline
    p95=0.3-0.4ms; DURING the pass p95=5.2-7.7ms, max=5.8-9.6ms. Comfortably
    under the 100ms target -- PASS.
  - Isolated to embedder.embed_query alone (no DB/LanceDB, ONNX only): idle
    p95=0.4-0.5ms; during embed p95=1.2-1.5ms, max=2.2-2.4ms. PASS, and
    confirms the (small) lag above is not concentrated in ONNX specifically.

INTERPRETATION: the passive related-notes worker is NOT the mechanism behind
the felt lag. It already runs off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread +
@work(exclusive=True) (structurally can't overlap -- a new pass cancels/
supersedes any still-running one), and the offloaded call (FTS5 + fastembed/
ONNX + LanceDB combined) yields the event loop well within the pass/fail
target. This is evidence AGAINST the prime suspect the lode-0wj debate raised:
lode-0wj.3 (disable/opt-in the passive pass) is likely a red herring as
currently scoped and should be re-evaluated against other candidates (Textual
render cost, TextArea internals, terminal I/O, something outside this pass)
before being treated as the fix -- lode-0wj.4 (optimise based on findings)
should look elsewhere first.

Caveat: this spike measured a *single* related-notes pass's cost per call, not
compounding effects from many other things happening concurrently in a real
long TUI session (job queue worker, reconciliation scan, etc.) -- if the felt
lag persists after lode-0wj.4 investigates other candidates, re-run this
spike's heartbeat instrumentation (now permanent, DEBUG-gated, in
lode.tui.latency_probe + lode.tui.screens.capture) against a live session to
see if some other component holds the GIL longer.

INSTRUMENTATION (permanent, toggleable, no behaviour change): DEBUG-level
logging in lode.tui.screens.capture around debounce restart/fire and each
related-notes pass (sequence number, duration, result count, whether it was
cancelled by a newer pass), plus lode.tui.latency_probe.probe_event_loop_lag,
an event-loop-lag heartbeat only started while
log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG). All gated behind LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
(existing lode.logconfig convention) -- zero log calls and zero extra worker
at the default INFO level.

Reproduction: LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1 pytest -s tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py

metadata.land_summary: Lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2): DEBUG-gated event-loop-lag instrumentation (lode.tui.latency_probe + capture screen) + opt-in seeded-corpus repro; verdict: fastembed/ONNX releases the GIL, related-notes pass is not the felt-lag cause. No behaviour change at INFO.

title: Confirm-on-unsaved guard for the capture screen's Escape (stop Escape silently discarding)
description: ASSUMED DECISION (proceeding without user confirm — revisit if wrong): scope to ESCAPE ONLY — fully screen-local, directly solves the vi-muscle-memory footgun. Escape on a dirty (non-empty/non-whitespace) capture buffer pops a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm; an empty buffer exits immediately so get-in/dump/get-out stays fast. Ctrl+S keeps its direct save+exit. The app-level Ctrl+Q confirm-if-dirty is SPLIT OUT to lode-0wj.8: Ctrl+Q is a global App binding (priority=True, src/lode/tui/app.py) and cannot be guarded from inside the capture screen. 'Dirty' == non-empty buffer today (capture only ever mints a NEW note; 'unchanged vs empty' only becomes a real distinction once lode-0wj.6 loads an existing version into the buffer).
acceptance_criteria: Escape on a non-empty/non-whitespace capture buffer shows a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm; Discard exits, Save saves+exits, Cancel returns to editing. Escape on an empty/whitespace-only buffer exits with no prompt. Ctrl+S behaviour unchanged. Tests cover dirty vs empty for Escape.

title: E14 — Post-E11 TUI feedback: exit safety, input latency, browse screen
description: Tracks user feedback gathered after E11 (TUI screens) shipped. Three themes from specs/01-feedback.md: (1) too easy to lose work — Escape silently discards the capture buffer (vi muscle-memory hits it), want a safer exit (Ctrl+Q and/or confirm-on-unsaved); (2) TUI is laggy — input feels blocked, need instrumentation to find the cause and optimisations (likely the passive related-notes pass and/or async task scheduling); (3) browsing interface — add an opt-in browse screen listing notes (Date/Version/Summary), selecting opens a note, Escape returns to the list; viewing prior versions deferred. Children filed under this epic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Neither Escape nor the app-level quit key can silently discard an unsaved capture buffer (scope of the quit-key guard resolved in lode-0wj.1). 2) The TUI has instrumentation that reveals what runs on the input path (incl. whether background passes actually yield the event loop), and at least one MEASURED optimisation lands against a defined latency threshold so typing no longer feels blocked. 3) A browse screen lists notes and lets the user open one and return, without adding overhead to the default get-in/dump/get-out capture path.
notes: Source: specs/01-feedback.md. Grounding: capture screen binds escape->discard (src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py); app binds ctrl+q->quit (src/lode/tui/app.py); passive related-notes runs ONNX embedder+LanceDB per idle pause via asyncio.to_thread.

title: Skeleton not end-to-end: restore synchronous inline embed in capture path; prove lode add -> lode ask via real CLI (no in-test stand-in)
description: GAP (found 2026-06-28): the Phase-A skeleton does NOT work end-to-end through the real CLI. "lode add" enqueues embed/enrich derive jobs (jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs, lode-y42.1) but NOTHING drains them: E2 (lode-i05.*) is unbuilt and embedding does NOT run inline either. A real "lode add" then "lode ask" therefore retrieves nothing (empty passages/vectors) and abstains. The exit-gate pass (lode-6w1.1) is masked: tests/test_skeleton_gate.py defines its own _run_derive_job() that runs embed() synchronously with a stub embedder INSIDE the test, so it never exercises any user-runnable processing step. This contradicts the epic (lode-6w1), which specified "synchronous inline embed (no queue yet)" for the skeleton: lode-x6r.2 built the embed(version) function and lode-x6r.5 is the deepening that MOVES it to the async queue once E2 exists. The build skipped ahead to enqueue-only without the drain. FIX (skeleton, simplest thing that works): make "lode add" run chunk+embed inline (lode-x6r.2 intent) so capture makes the note findable; keep the durable embed/enrich enqueue as the E2 seam but do NOT make the skeleton ask depend on a worker. Then replace the in-test stand-in with a CLI-level test that proves a real "lode add" followed by "lode ask" yields a verbatim-grounded cited claim and that an out-of-corpus question abstains. Do NOT build the full async worker here: that stays E2 (lode-i05.3, P2) and the inline->async move stays lode-x6r.5.

title: Save-on-exit confirm should be a popup over the editor, not a blank full screen
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 4: when the user presses Esc (or Ctrl+Q) over a dirty capture buffer, the Save/Discard/Cancel prompt appears on an otherwise blank screen. It should instead be a popup window centered over the still-visible editor, dismissed (returning to the editor unchanged) on Cancel — less jarring and closer to normal UI conventions.

Root cause: src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py DiscardConfirmScreen is a bare ModalScreen with NO styling, and the repo has no TUI CSS at all (no .tcss anywhere). Without CSS the dialog isn't sized/centered and the backdrop isn't styled, so it reads as a blank screen with a prompt.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04)
Ship an external Textual .tcss stylesheet (NOT DEFAULT_CSS) — this establishes the repo's TUI stylesheet pattern. That means three coordinated pieces:
1. A .tcss file (e.g. src/lode/tui/screens/capture.tcss, or an app-level src/lode/tui/lode.tcss) styling DiscardConfirmScreen: a centered, bounded, bordered dialog box floating over the capture editor, with the editor visible/dimmed behind it.
2. Wire it: set CSS_PATH on LodeApp (src/lode/tui/app.py) — or the screen's CSS_PATH — to load the file.
3. PACKAGE it: add the .tcss to [tool.setuptools.package-data] in pyproject.toml. Today that section only has: lode = ["*.sql"]. package-data keys are per-package and non-recursive, so add an entry that actually covers the .tcss's location (e.g. "lode.tui.screens" = ["*.tcss"], or a recursive lode = ["**/*.sql", "**/*.tcss"] if using recursive globs). MISS THIS and it works from a source checkout but the INSTALLED WHEEL ships without the stylesheet — a bug nox will not catch.

Before styling, verify the pinned Textual version's ModalScreen default background: if it already dims/shows the screen below, the only fix needed is sizing+centering the dialog box; if it does not, ALSO set a translucent backdrop so the editor is visible behind the box rather than a black void.

## Acceptance Criteria
- DiscardConfirmScreen renders as a centered, bounded, bordered dialog floating over the capture editor, with the editor visible (dimmed) behind it — not a full blank screen.
- The stylesheet is an external .tcss loaded via CSS_PATH, and pyproject [tool.setuptools.package-data] is updated to ship it; verify the built wheel/sdist actually contains the .tcss (e.g. inspect 'python -m build' output or the installed tree), not just a source run.
- Cancel (c / Escape) dismisses the dialog and returns to the editor with the buffer untouched (existing _on_discard_confirm behavior preserved); Save (s) and Discard (d) keep current semantics.
- Existing tests (tests/test_tui_capture_confirm.py) still pass; add coverage that the confirm is an overlay — the CaptureScreen below stays mounted on the screen stack while the dialog is up.
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Refines lode-0wj.1 (Escape guard) / lode-0wj.8 (Ctrl+Q guard) from epic lode-0wj. Touches src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py, a new .tcss, src/lode/tui/app.py (CSS_PATH), and pyproject.toml (package-data) — independent of the logging children (.1/.2/.3).

metadata.land_summary: Save-on-exit DiscardConfirmScreen is now a centered, bordered popup over the still-visible (dimmed) editor via the repo's first external Textual stylesheet (src/lode/tui/lode.tcss, loaded through LodeApp.CSS_PATH and shipped via pyproject package-data 'lode.tui'=['*.tcss']).

title: Add top-level 'lode --debug' flag to enable diagnostic instrumentation
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 2: there should be a --debug flag for the CLI that enables debugging features (e.g. the event-loop-lag probe). Today those features are only reachable via LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG; there is no CLI flag.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04)
TOP-LEVEL flag on the root Typer callback (src/lode/cli.py main()): 'lode --debug <subcommand>' sets the log level to DEBUG and thereby enables the diagnostic instrumentation already gated on DEBUG (e.g. lode.tui.latency_probe via CaptureScreen, gated on log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)). Applies to every subcommand (tui/ask/add/...), not just tui. Wiring is sound: configure_logging sets the ROOT logger to DEBUG, and child loggers (lode.tui.screens.capture, etc.) inherit that effective level, so the probe gate turns on.

Known, accepted coupling: --debug == 'set log level to DEBUG'. This ties log VERBOSITY to feature ENABLEMENT (the probe). Consistent with the existing latency_probe design decision to reuse the DEBUG toggle every lode module already logs behind (see latency_probe.py docstring), so we accept it now. If a future debug feature must be enabled WITHOUT DEBUG-level log spam (or vice-versa), split the two concepts then.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'lode --debug tui' (and other subcommands) runs at DEBUG log level, turning on the event-loop-lag probe and other DEBUG-gated instrumentation.
- Without --debug, behavior is unchanged; LODE_LOG_LEVEL is still honored as the env fallback, and --debug takes precedence when passed.
- Interplay with TUI-only file logging (lode-1i8.2): in the TUI, --debug raises verbosity in the log FILE only — console stays suppressed (the TUI never echoes to the terminal, debug or not). For plain CLI commands, --debug raises verbosity on the existing stderr + file handlers (console stays available for the CLI).
- The flag is documented as the switch for diagnostic instrumentation. NOTE: to avoid colliding with lode-1i8.1 on docs/configuration.md, this ticket depends on .1; document --debug by ADDING to the logging section .1 creates (or in CLI --help), not by racing the same file.
- Tests cover the callback wiring (DEBUG level applied when --debug set; env fallback otherwise).
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Touches src/lode/cli.py main() callback and the configure_logging call. Depends on lode-1i8.2 (shared logconfig/cli files) AND lode-1i8.1 (shared docs/configuration.md) — build after both land.

metadata.land_summary: Add top-level 'lode --debug' flag on the root Typer callback: resolves to an explicit DEBUG log level (precedence over the LODE_LOG_LEVEL env fallback), enabling every DEBUG-gated diagnostic (e.g. the TUI latency_probe) across all subcommands; threaded through ctx.obj so tui's file-only reconfigure (lode-1i8.2) re-applies DEBUG without reattaching the console handler. Docs row + 5 tests. Technical review: no fixes needed, gates green.

title: TUI-only file logging: suppress console log output while the TUI runs (keep file handler)
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 3: debug logging correctly writes to the log file, but ALSO dumps to the console, which corrupts the Textual TUI. This blocks the current exercise of collecting latency telemetry from the TUI.

Root cause: src/lode/logconfig.py configure_logging() calls logging.basicConfig(level, format), which attaches a stderr StreamHandler in addition to the file handler from _attach_file_handler. Both are live, so every log record echoes to the terminal. configure_logging() is called once, in the top-level Typer callback (cli.py:73), for ALL commands.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04, re-scoped after debate)
TUI-ONLY console suppression. Do NOT drop stderr logging globally: plain CLI commands (ask/add/...) legitimately use stderr — notably 'lode ask' deliberately relies on the root logger mirroring to stderr to surface an AuthError's cause (see cli.py ~260-269 and its comment). That path must keep working unchanged.

Instead, only the TUI runs file-only:
- When 'lode tui' launches, suppress console/stderr log output for the TUI session (remove the stderr StreamHandler basicConfig added from the root logger), keeping ONLY the file handler.
- MUST guarantee a file handler is attached for the TUI session so that, with no stream handler present, Python's last-resort handler (logging.lastResort, WARNING+ to stderr) can never fire and re-corrupt the display. The callback already attaches the file handler via log_dir(); the TUI path must ensure it remains/attaches, not merely remove the stream handler.

Suggested shape (builder's discretion): either the 'tui' command calls a small helper (e.g. in logconfig) that detaches root stream handlers and asserts the file handler, or configure_logging grows a console: bool flag the tui command passes as False. Keep it simple.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running 'lode tui' emits ZERO log output to the terminal at any level (INFO or DEBUG) — verified by observation; this is a manual/observational check, NOT an automatable assertion (a live TUI owns the alternate screen).
- The AUTOMATABLE acceptance is structural: after the TUI configures logging, assert the root logger has no stream/console handler AND has the lode file handler (so records land in the file, not lastResort→stderr). Cover in tests/test_logconfig.py (or a tui logging test).
- Plain CLI behavior is UNCHANGED: 'lode ask'/'lode add' still mirror logs to stderr; the cli.py AuthError stderr-mirroring path and its comment remain valid (do not edit that comment).
- Log records still land in $LODE_HOME/logs/lode.log (format unchanged) so latency telemetry is collectible via the file.
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Touches src/lode/logconfig.py (+ the 'tui' command in cli.py, or tui/app.py). BLOCKS lode-1i8.3 (--debug) since both edit logconfig/cli — build .2 first. Telemetry collection is unblocked by THIS ticket alone (set LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG + file-only TUI); the --debug flag (.3) is a convenience on top.

metadata.land_summary: TUI-only file logging: configure_logging grows a keyword-only console flag; the tui command calls it with console=False to strip the stderr stream handler while keeping the file handler (never handler-less, so lastResort can't fire). Plain CLI stderr logging unchanged.

title: init_db missing next_attempt_at migration: pre-2f2379d jobs tables crash lode work
description: A jobs table created before commit 2f2379d (schema hardening) lacks the next_attempt_at column. schema.sql's CREATE TABLE has it for fresh DBs, but storage.py _apply_migrations never added a matching ALTER, so existing DBs are never upgraded. Result: 'lode work' -> _batch_submit_enrich -> OperationalError: no such column: next_attempt_at. Fix: add nullable ADD COLUMN (SQLite rejects an expression default) + backfill next_attempt_at=created for NULL rows so pre-existing jobs become due.

metadata.land_summary: migrate jobs.next_attempt_at onto pre-existing DBs (nullable add + backfill)

title: Add kind='summary' AI enrichment — Haiku one-line note summary
description: Browse (lode-0wj.5) shows a Summary column, but no summary exists today: enrich (src/lode/enrich.py) produces only kind=tag/entity/edge. Add a new WHOLE-NOTE AI annotation kind='summary' — a one-line Haiku-derived summary of the note's head version — by EXTENDING the existing extract_enrichment tool (not a new job type): add a 'summary' field to the tool schema + prompt, bump ENRICH_PROMPT_VER, and write it to the annotations table (source='ai', kind='summary', target=note_id, source_version=head) with the same full provenance (model, prompt_ver, created) and idempotent source_version-keyed replace as tag/entity. title: Optimise TUI input latency based on instrumentation findings
description: Follow-up to the instrumentation spike: apply the measured optimisation(s) so typing no longer feels blocked. Candidate directions the user raised: better async isolation, deferring background tasks, or manual-instead-of-auto task runs for the async work queue. Scope firms up once the spike reports where the input path actually blocks. Depends on the diagnosis ticket.
acceptance_criteria: At least one measured optimisation lands; keystroke->render latency measurably improved vs the spike's baseline; typing no longer blocks on background work.
notes:
SPIKE VERDICT (lode-0wj.2, ready-for-land): the passive related-notes worker is NOT the felt-lag source — fastembed/ONNX releases the GIL, asyncio.to_thread is relieving input as designed, event-loop lag stayed single-digit ms vs the 100ms target. So the optimisation should look ELSEWHERE than the related-notes/embedder path (that path is already non-blocking). Re-scope against the other candidate directions before building; the spike's instrumentation (LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG heartbeat + capture.py debug logs) is the tool to localise the real blocker.
BUILD (lode-0wj.4): re-scoped per the lode-0wj.2 verdict -- looked elsewhere
than embedder inference, which the spike already cleared. Live-diagnosed the
REAL CaptureScreen (driven through Textual's pilot against the lode-5y8.4 seed
corpus, real embedder -- not an isolated find_related_notes() call) and found
capture.py never passed an embedder into find_related_notes, so every
debounce-fired pass built a *fresh* FastEmbedEmbedder and reloaded the ONNX
model from scratch. Measured: ~1.5s of event-loop stall per pause in typing,
every pause, for the whole session -- ONNX model *construction* (unlike
inference) does not release the GIL.

FIX: CaptureScreen._ensure_embedder constructs one embedder and reuses it for
the screen's lifetime (src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py); FastEmbedEmbedder._load
gets a lock (src/lode/lode/embedding.py) since reuse makes concurrent-thread
access to one instance real for the first time. MEASURED RESULT: pass #1 in a
session still pays ~1.3s (unavoidable first load), pass #2+ measures ~90ms with
zero event-loop-starvation warnings -- matching the spike's single-digit-ms
inference verdict. ~14x improvement on the repeat case, which is the common
case in any real typing session longer than one pause.

Tried and reverted: eagerly warming the embedder at screen mount (so even pass
#1 would be fast). Reverted because it made every CaptureScreen mount pay a
real ONNX load unconditionally -- broke tests/test_tui_quit.py's
Ctrl+Q-discard test by giving the debounce timer enough real wall-clock time to
fire mid-test. Scoped back to lazy reuse-on-first-use only (docstring on
_ensure_embedder records why).

Tests: tests/test_tui_app.py::test_embedder_is_constructed_once_and_reused_across_multiple_passes
pins the fix (construction count == 1 across 3 debounce-fired passes with a
stub embedder). Full suite green (702 passed, 7 skipped).

title: Restore synchronous FTS5 on the capture path (regression from x6r.5)
description:
E3's core invariant is violated on trunk after lode-x6r.5: the FTS5 lexical index must be written SYNCHRONOUSLY on save so a just-captured note is keyword-findable BEFORE any async work runs (x6r.4 AC; docs/retrieval.md 'sync, always fresh'; the vector leg is allowed to lag precisely BECAUSE the lexical leg is fresh). On trunk neither leg is synchronous.

ROOT CAUSE: x6r.5 (move EMBEDDING off the capture path) deleted cli._embed_inline, which bundled BOTH the model-bearing vector leg AND the model-FREE FTS lexical leg. Moving embedding async was correct; moving FTS async was over-reach — FTS being model-free is the whole reason the design keeps it synchronous (instant keyword-findability, no model wait). Now the only FTS write is in worker._embed_handler (worker.py:304-330), reached only when 'lode work' drains the embed job. Compounding it: cli.py add (cli.py:138) builds Repository(conn) with NO cache => NullCache() (repository.py:137), so Repository.save's post-commit self.cache.index() is a no-op. The CompositeCache + FTS CacheBackend machinery built by lode-1f9 was never injected into the capture path — pre-x6r.5 the sync FTS was carried only by the _embed_inline skeleton stand-in, which x6r.5 removed.

EFFECT: 'lode add' then immediately 'lode ask' finds nothing by keyword until 'lode work' runs. The design's retrieval-correctness argument no longer holds.

MISSED BECAUSE: x6r.5 rewired the skeleton-gate tests from add->ask to add->work->ask, masking the regression; there is no test for x6r.4's actual AC (FTS-findable before any async work).

FIX (Option A, ratified by bildzeitung 2026-06-29 debate of lode-x6r):
- Inject the real CompositeCache — with the FTS lexical CacheBackend (lode-1f9) — into the Repository that cli.py add uses, so Repository.save writes passages + FTS5 rows SYNCHRONOUSLY after the version commit (chunking and FTS are model-free; safe in the capture path).
- Keep EMBEDDING async: the worker stays the sole embedder; do NOT re-introduce synchronous embedding (preserve x6r.5's capture-latency win).
- Make worker._embed_handler vector-only (drop its FTS leg) OR keep FTS idempotent so the worker never double-indexes; the capture-path sync write is the source of the invariant.
- KEY COUPLING to resolve: i05.4's reconciliation embed-gap query keys off 'head version with no passages row'. If passages are now written synchronously on save, that signal no longer detects a missing VECTOR. Re-key the embed-gap signal to 'head version with no vectors' (or equivalent) so reconciliation still re-enqueues embeds correctly. Verify the i05.1 atomic save+enqueue and i05.4 reconcile still behave.
- Record the settled capture-path composition (CompositeCache injected; passages+FTS synchronous, embedding async) in docs/ (storage.md / retrieval.md), in a worktree.
design: Inject CompositeCache (FTS CacheBackend from lode-1f9, + the LanceDB vector backend) into Repository in cli.py add. Repository.save already drives self.cache.index() post-commit (repository.py:170) — wiring a real composite there gives synchronous passages+FTS. Embedding stays in worker._embed_handler. Split the legs: model-free (chunk + passages + FTS) = synchronous on save via the cache seam; model-bearing (embed -> LanceDB vectors) = async via the worker. Then fix the i05.4 reconcile gap query to key off missing vectors, not missing passages.
acceptance_criteria: A note saved via 'lode add' is keyword-findable via FTS5 BEFORE 'lode work' runs — 'lode ask' on a keyword in the note returns it with no intervening 'lode work'. Embedding remains async (the vector leg still requires the worker). A regression test asserts add -> ask (no work) finds the note by keyword (this is x6r.4's real AC, currently untested). The worker does not double-index FTS. The reconciliation embed-gap signal (i05.4) still correctly detects a missing vector now that passages are written synchronously. The capture-path cache composition is recorded in docs/.

metadata.land_summary: Restore synchronous FTS5 on capture: cli.py add injects CompositeCache([LexicalCacheBackend]) so Repository.save writes passages+passages_fts synchronously post-commit (keyword-findable before any async work); worker._embed_handler is now vector-only (no double-index); i05.4 reconcile embed-gap signal re-keyed from 'no passages row' to 'no non-dead embed job' (passages now exist on save). New Gate 4 (add->ask, no work, FTS finds + cites) and Gate 5 (worker doesn't double-index FTS) regression tests; reconcile tests cover passages-alone-not-a-gap + dead-job re-enqueue. Docs updated (storage.md/retrieval.md). Code review: clean, no changes needed. Gates green: 448 passed, 4 skipped.

title: Wire vector store as a CacheBackend + cache-engine composition (Repository)
description:
Route cache access THROUGH the Repository interface (lode-s2f.5) and resolve how multiple regenerable-cache engines coexist in the Repository's single cache slot. Deferred out of lode-x6r.3 (LanceDB vector store), which built the standalone VectorStore engine but did NOT wire it as a CacheBackend because doing so forces this composition decision before the FTS leg exists.

Scope:
- Make the vector store reachable via the Repository CacheBackend Protocol (index/evict -> chunk+embed+VectorStore.replace_vectors / drop), so callers reach vectors through Repository, not lode.embedding directly. This satisfies the 'access is through the repository interface' criterion that x6r.3 deferred.
- Decide + implement the COMPOSITION: the Repository takes one 'cache' slot, but the cache has multiple engines — passage vectors (LanceDB, x6r.3), the FTS5 lexical index (x6r.4), and later the networkx knowledge graph. Likely a composite CacheBackend that fans index/evict out to each engine. Settle this so x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save) plugs into the same mechanism rather than inventing its own.
- Keep it the simplest thing that works (docs/stack.md 'keep the cache behind a repository interface'); record any settled composition decision in docs/ (stack.md/storage.md), not only code.
acceptance_criteria: Vector (and the FTS) cache engine is driven through the Repository CacheBackend; a composite/multiplexing backend fans head-change index/evict to each engine; callers reach the cache only through Repository, not the engine modules directly.
notes: NEXT-SESSION SEQUENCING (handoff 2026-06-23): build this SOLO and FIRST. It is the E3 lynchpin — it settles the composite CacheBackend that BOTH x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save, now dep-gated on this) and the eventual E4 retrieval wiring plug into. Touches the repository.py seam + embedding.py/vectorstore.py, so it does not parallelize cleanly with other E3 work. The only safe sibling to fan out alongside it is lode-5y8.3 (golden Q&A set — disjoint files, but carries its own open metric-weighting question). After 1f9 lands, x6r.4 becomes ready and plugs FTS into the settled composite. Record the composition decision in docs/ (stack.md/storage.md), not only code.

title: Harden bd↔git sync: jsonl post-checkout hook reverts bd writes on rebase
description: REPRODUCIBLE: a bd close/label change made in a session is silently reverted when a later 'git pull --rebase' runs. Root cause: core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks; the post-checkout/post-merge hooks call 'bd hooks run', which reconciles Dolt FROM the working-tree .beads/issues.jsonl. 'git pull --rebase' checks out intermediate commits whose exported jsonl still shows the pre-close state (in_progress + ready-for-land), so post-checkout re-imports that and reverts the Dolt close. Hit 3x (lode-8bh, lode-wvf, lode-bxz). Contradicts the stated model (Dolt authoritative, jsonl passive). WORKAROUND that holds: after bd writes, 'bd dolt push' first, then export+commit jsonl once, then PLAIN 'git push' (no --rebase). Proper fix: make the flow Dolt-authoritative end-to-end — bake ordering into the producer/lander/coding agent defs + CLAUDE.md session-close (which currently mandates 'git pull --rebase'); consider ff-only pulls and/or disabling the jsonl→Dolt import on checkout. Blocks reliable landing — the whole landing loop rests on 'ready-for-land lives in beads'.

title: lode add (capture + save)
description: Capture a note from CLI and persist via versions.save(); enqueue derive jobs. Instant, no AI in the path.
design: lode add = capture/create. Mint a fresh uuid4 note_id (logical id, no aliasing), read body from positional TEXT arg or stdin (verbatim; reject empty/whitespace-only). Open DB via init_db at --db (envvar LODE_DB, default ~/.local/share/lode/lode.db). Call versions.save() (always a create) — NO AI in path. On HeadConflictError write the rejected buffer to a unique draft file beside the DB, print 'note changed since opened' + draft path, exit 1 (never clobber/auto-merge). On success enqueue derive jobs (pending embed+enrich rows) via new thin lode.jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs in its own txn; reconciliation scan (docs/storage.md) is the self-healing net for the save/enqueue gap since the lane fence forbids editing versions.py to make it one txn. Lane: cli.py + test_cli.py + new jobs.py + test_jobs.py only.
acceptance_criteria: lode add captures a note and persists via save() with no AI call in the path, enqueues derive jobs, and on CAS reject writes a draft + prints the diff path.
notes: CAS-reject UX (CLI-first phase, since the interactive reconciliation UI is E11/TUI): on a CAS rejection, 'lode add' writes the rejected buffer to a draft file and prints the diff path + 'note changed since opened'; full interactive re-apply/discard waits for E11. title: versions.save() — CAS head, no-op dedup, op tombstone
description: save(): write immutable version row + move head via compare-and-swap (reject if head moved); no-op dedup vs head body; op = create/update/delete (tombstone); soft-delete recovery = repoint head.
design: versions.save() over the s2f.1 schema + s2f.2 hashing. Single primitive save(conn,note_id,body,*,parent,settings) that creates (note absent -> op=create, parent=NO_PARENT, atomic note+root-version insert via DEFERRABLE FK) or updates (note present -> CAS: parent must==current head). No-op dedup: body==head body returns the head, writes no row. delete(conn,note_id,*,parent) tombstones (op=delete, carries head body forward, CAS-moves head). recover(conn,note_id,*,target_version) repoints head to a prior version (no new row). CAS reject raises HeadConflictError(note_id,expected_parent,actual_head) — the clean seam s2f.4 extends into the diff/buffer-preserve conflict surface; NOT implementing that surface here. import content_version_id from lode.hashing (single source of truth).
acceptance_criteria: save() rejects a write whose parent != current head (CAS); a save with body identical to head returns the head and writes NO new row (no-op dedup); delete writes a tombstone op preserving lineage; head can be repointed to recover a soft-deleted note.

metadata.land_summary: lode.versions: save() (create/update with head CAS + no-op dedup), delete() (op=delete tombstone, body carried forward), recover() (repoint head); HeadConflictError seam left for s2f.4. Imports content_version_id from hashing. 11 tests, gates green.

(a) Ratify consumer-owned persistence: land s2f.4 as-is (storage returns the preserved buffer; CLI/E11 persist the draft) and add a docs/storage.md line pinning the layer split so it isn't code-only. (Reviewer leans here.)

Branch origin/land/lode-s2f.4 @ 5062f4f is KEPT for the human.

title: hashing.py — framed xxh3-128 content-address hash
description: Length-prefixed framed H (xxh3-128, blake2b-128 stdlib fallback) for version_id=H(framed:note_id,parent,body) and snapshot_id. Unit-test the framing-ambiguity cases (H('a','bc') != H('ab','c')) per docs/storage.md.
design:
OWNS lode's canonical content-hash encoding — this is a STORAGE decision, ratified here, NOT by the eval seed fixture (see lode-5y8.4 escalation resolved 2026-06-23 -> option b). Beyond the hash code, two deliverables:

acceptance_criteria: Unit tests prove framing is unambiguous: H('a','bc') != H('ab','c'); version_id = H(framed:note_id,parent,body) is reproducible for identical inputs; blake2b-128 fallback path exercised.

title: Add 'build' to the dev extra for a canonical wheel/sdist packaging path
description:
The repo has no packaging/build tool in its dev deps, so there is no canonical way to produce or verify a wheel/sdist. 'python -m build' (PyPA's standard front-end for setuptools.build_meta, which is already the [build-system] backend) is the obvious tool and is exactly what lode-1i8.4's acceptance criterion assumed: 'verify the built wheel/sdist actually contains the .tcss (e.g. inspect python -m build output)'. But 'build' is not installed.

CONTEXT: hit during /epic-audit of lode-1i8 — I went to run 'python -m build --wheel' to confirm the TUI stylesheet actually ships in the wheel (the package-data footgun lode-1i8.4 flagged) and it failed with 'No module named build'; I fell back to 'pip wheel . --no-deps' (works, but is not the standard/reproducible packaging path and doesn't exercise the sdist).

## Design
Add 'build' to [project.optional-dependencies].dev in pyproject.toml (alongside pytest/nox/ruff), unpinned per the repo's current 'unpinned until the build starts' convention. That makes 'python -m build' available in ./venv so packaging (wheel + sdist) is a first-class, reproducible operation and package-data regressions (like the .tcss shipping) can be verified the way the tickets already assume.

Optional (builder's discretion, keep it simple): a small nox session (e.g. 'nox -s build' or a package-data smoke check) that builds the wheel and asserts expected data files (*.sql, *.tcss) are present — turning the lode-1i8.4-class footgun into an automated gate instead of a manual inspection. Only add this if it stays lightweight; the dep itself is the core ask.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'build' is listed in the dev extra in pyproject.toml (unpinned, consistent with pytest/nox/ruff).
- After ./scripts/python-init.sh + activate, 'python -m build' produces a wheel AND an sdist with no missing-module error.
- The built wheel contains the shipped package-data (src/lode/schema.sql -> lode/schema.sql and src/lode/tui/lode.tcss -> lode/tui/lode.tcss).
- nox -t fix passes; if a build/smoke nox session is added, it passes too.

## Notes
Touches pyproject.toml (dev extra). Docs/deps-only; no runtime code. Independent of lode-1i8.* (that epic is audited); this is standalone dev-tooling.
acceptance_criteria: 'build' is in the pyproject dev extra; 'python -m build' yields a wheel+sdist post python-init; the wheel contains lode/schema.sql and lode/tui/lode.tcss; nox -t fix passes.

title: Enrich gap: empty-summary heads thrash reconcile (stamp job prompt_ver in worker)
description: Surfaced during lode-0wj.9 review. title: Wire redact-before-index into the actual save/index path
description:
lode-fk8.2 built redact_before_index() (src/lode/redact.py) as a pure, unit-tested function, but it has zero callers outside its own test file. docs/externals.md's "Two redactions, aimed at the right legs" is explicit that a pasted .env/API key must not become locally retrievable via vector or FTS search -- but today it does:

- cli.py `add` -> Repository.save(note_id, body) stores the raw body, no redaction call.
- embedding.py:embed() reads the raw body via _version_body() and calls chunk() directly -- no redact_before_index() call before chunking/embedding into LanceDB.
- lexical.py:LexicalIndex.replace_passages() also chunks the raw body directly into passages_fts -- no redaction there either.

redact-before-egress (the enrich/Q&A leg) is correctly wired via lode.egress.gate_qa_egress and enrich.py -- only the before-index leg was left unconnected. Found during a /debate completeness pass on lode-fk8 prior to closing the epic.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `lode add "key: TOPSECRET-42 done"` (or any text matching a redact_before_index_patterns seed).
2. Vector- or keyword-search (`lode ask` context retrieval, or a direct FTS/LanceDB query) for `TOPSECRET-42`.
3. Observe the secret is retrievable -- it was never stripped before chunking/embedding/FTS indexing.

Most natural fix point: apply redact_before_index() to the body once in Repository.save (or equivalent shared point) before it is handed to embedding.embed() and LexicalIndex.replace_passages(), so both indexing legs see the same redacted text. title: immediate Haiku on save + Batches API for bulk (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-npx.2, bounced by /land semantic review.

ORIGINAL: Fresh note enriches via one immediate Haiku call; bulk/backfill/re-enrich via
the 50%-off Batches API (uses E2 batch-resume). embed always lands fast regardless.

REBUILD BRIEF (from land-review):

Acceptance: The ticket's contract is "A fresh note enriches via one immediate Haiku
call" — the note just saved, specifically. cli.py::_enrich_immediately(conn, db_path,
version_id) takes a version_id parameter and its docstring claims it "opportunistically
claim[s] + run[s] the enrich job just enqueued for version_id" — but the body never uses
version_id; it calls worker.claim_and_run_one(conn, db_path, Settings(),
types=("enrich",)), which claims via _claim_one: oldest pending job of type enrich,
FIFO, no filter by version/target at all (src/lode/worker.py _claim_one).

If any other enrich job is already pending at the moment of `add` — a backlog from a
burst of prior adds, an idle/offline worker, jobs not yet swept by
_batch_submit_enrich's flush-size-limited pass — the freshly saved note's own job stays
pending and an unrelated, older note gets the immediate Haiku call instead. The new note
is silently NOT enriched immediately, contradicting the acceptance criterion as written.
This isn't hypothetical: the bounced branch's own commit 10b1d36 ("fix(enrich): close
batch-submit vs immediate-enrich double-spend TOCTOU") describes exactly this —
"an interactive `lode add` immediate-enrich (claim_and_run_one, which runs without the
worker lock) can flip a job pending->running between the batch step's SELECT and its
UPDATE" — the branch's own author relied on claim_and_run_one grabbing an arbitrary
pending job to explain the TOCTOU it then had to fix.

Test coverage masked this: every test in test_cli.py starts from an empty DB, so the
job just enqueued is always the only pending enrich job and happens to be the one
claimed — the tests can't distinguish "claims the job for this note" from "claims
whatever's oldest." No test exercised a backlog at time of `add`.

docs/storage.md's "How the immediate path stays a fast path" section states the capture
path "claims and runs that specific job inline" — documents the same false invariant as
the code; needs correcting too.

WHAT THE REBUILD MUST SATISFY:
1. _enrich_immediately must claim the SPECIFIC job it just enqueued for version_id, not
   an arbitrary oldest-pending enrich job. Options: (a) have save()/
   enqueue_derive_jobs return the enrich job's row id and add a claim-by-id primitive
   (CAS UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status='pending', mirroring _claim_one but keyed on id
   instead of type-priority scan), or (b) filter claim_and_run_one's candidate query by
   target_version.
2. Correct docs/storage.md's "that specific job" claim to match reality (or make it true).
3. Add a regression test that seeds an unrelated pending enrich job before calling `add`
   and asserts the NEW note's job — not the backlog one — ends up 'done'.
4. Carry over what was sound in the bounced branch: the atomic embed+enrich enqueue in
   Repository.save, the double-spend CAS fix for batch-submit vs immediate-enrich
   (commit 10b1d36's mechanism), and the Batches API bulk path — all reviewed clean and
   should not be redone from scratch.

Bounced branch for reference: land/lode-npx.2 @ 10b1d369a3b9afa7a03a3cb19ca3f5d9eb7a9b9f
(dropped from origin as part of this bounce).
acceptance_criteria: A fresh note's enrich job (not an arbitrary pending backlog job) is the one claimed and run inline by lode add's immediate-enrich path, verified by a regression test that seeds an unrelated pending enrich job first; docs/storage.md's description of the immediate-claim mechanism matches the implementation; the atomic embed+enrich enqueue, the batch-submit/immediate-enrich double-spend CAS fix, and the Batches API bulk path from the bounced branch are preserved.

Threads keyword-only target_version through worker._claim_one (adds 'AND target_version = ?' to the candidate SELECT) and worker.claim_and_run_one; cli._enrich_immediately passes result.version_id. Carried over clean: atomic embed+enrich enqueue, batch-vs-immediate double-spend per-row CAS, Batches API bulk path. docs/storage.md immediate-claim invariant corrected. title: Wire rerank + graph_expand into the live retrieve() pipeline (cli._retrieve)
description:
Context: found during /land semantic review of lode-72m.5 (graph_expand + trust_rank).

E4's own epic-level acceptance criteria (lode-72m) reads: "hybrid retrieval runs
FTS5 + vector -> RRF -> rerank -> expand_parents -> graph_expand -> trust_rank
over passages, heads only." With lode-72m.5 landed, all 5 subtasks are closed
and the epic reads 5/5 -- but the live `lode ask` path (cli.py's private
`_retrieve`) only calls: lexical_search + vector_search -> reciprocal_rank_fusion
-> expand_parents -> trust_rank. Two of the six documented stages are never
invoked from the live path:

- `rerank()` (lode-72m.3, closed) -- built, unit-tested, config-gated via
  `Settings.rerank_enabled` (default on) -- but `_retrieve` never imports or
  calls it.
- `graph_expand()` (lode-72m.5, closed) -- same story: built, unit-tested,
  no-ops safely with no edges -- but `_retrieve` never calls it either.

Neither subtask's own (narrower) acceptance criteria mentioned wiring into
cli.py, so neither branch was bounced for it -- but the epic's acceptance is
not actually met, and nothing currently tracks closing that gap now that all
named subtasks are closed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `lode ask <question>` against a DB with edges and multiple candidate
   passages.
2. Read `src/lode/cli.py`'s `_retrieve` function.
3. Observe it imports only `build_match_query, expand_parents, lexical_search,
   reciprocal_rank_fusion, trust_rank, vector_search` from `lode.retrieval` --
   `rerank` and `graph_expand` are absent, so results are never reranked and
   the knowledge graph is never traversed, regardless of `Settings.rerank_enabled`
   or edge data present.
design: Depends on lode-72m (parent epic, for context) but is independent of any single closed subtask -- this closes the wiring gap left across lode-72m.3 and lode-72m.5.
acceptance_criteria: cli._retrieve calls rerank(...) (respecting Settings.rerank_enabled) between reciprocal_rank_fusion and expand_parents, and graph_expand(...) between expand_parents and trust_rank -- matching the full pipeline order in lode-72m's epic description and docs/retrieval.md. An integration test against the live 'lode ask' path (not just the individual retrieval.py unit tests) demonstrates both stages actually fire.

title: jobs schema hardening: idempotency key + backoff/dead-letter columns
description: The landed E1 jobs table (src/lode/schema.sql) cannot support the E2 acceptance criteria ('idempotent by key', 'backoff-retry -> dead-letter') as written. Harden the schema BEFORE the jobs-table/enqueue and worker-loop work so those tickets build on a sound table. Surfaced by the 2026-06-28 debate of E1 as the E2 foundation (see lode-i05 notes, findings 1/2/6).
design:
Three schema changes to src/lode/schema.sql + a docs/storage.md pin. Decisions PINNED 2026-06-28 (lode-i05 breakdown) — this supersedes the earlier "decide and pin" forks.

(1) IDEMPOTENCY KEY — a partial UNIQUE index over an expression.
Add a key expressing job identity so enqueue (i05.1) AND reconciliation re-enqueue (i05.4) is a no-op against an existing LIVE job, not a duplicate row. Identity is (type, target_version) for embed and (type, target_version, prompt_ver) for enrich. prompt_ver is NULL on embed and SQLite treats NULLs as DISTINCT in UNIQUE, so a naive UNIQUE(type,target_version,prompt_ver) will NOT dedupe embed jobs. Use a partial unique index over a COALESCE expression, scoped to live jobs:
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_jobs_live ON jobs(type, target_version, COALESCE(prompt_ver, ''))
        WHERE status IN ('pending', 'running');
Scoping to pending/running is load-bearing: it dedupes in-flight work, but STILL ALLOWS a re-enqueue after the prior job reached 'done'/'dead' — a prompt_ver bump or a re-derive must be able to enqueue again (the reconciliation scan depends on this). Enqueue switches to INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Also fix docs/storage.md:264, which omits `type` from the key formula.

(2) BACKOFF SCHEDULING — next_attempt_at.
Add `next_attempt_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(...'now'))` (ISO-8601 UTC) so the worker (i05.3) durably schedules a retry: a claim selects WHERE status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now. Without it a restart mid-backoff retries immediately.

(3) DEAD-LETTER TERMINAL — distinct 'dead' status (DECISION: distinct 'dead', NOT "'failed' is terminal").
Add 'dead' to the status CHECK so the enum is ('pending','running','done','failed','dead'). 'dead' is the poison terminal reached at the max-attempts gate; 'failed' is the transient last-error state a retry resets to 'pending' from. Update src/lode/cli.py (the `status` read-out, ~line 411, which today labels 'failed' as the dead-letter) to surface 'dead' as the dead-letter terminal. Record the status lifecycle pending -> running -> {done | failed -> pending | dead} in docs/storage.md, and update the §8 jobs status enum in the data-shape sketch (storage.md:342, currently pending|running|done|failed).

SCOPE FENCE: schema + docs + the cli.py status-label fix only. Does NOT fold enqueue into the save txn (i05.1), does NOT move enqueue ownership (i05.1), does NOT write the worker loop (i05.3). Update tests/ for the new constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A duplicate enqueue of the same LIVE (type,target_version[,prompt_ver]) is a no-op for BOTH embed (NULL prompt_ver) and enrich; a re-enqueue after the prior job is 'done'/'dead' IS allowed; jobs has next_attempt_at and 'dead' in the status CHECK; cli.py status read-out surfaces 'dead' as the dead-letter; docs/storage.md §8 + the async-queue section record the corrected (type-inclusive) idempotency key, next_attempt_at, and the pending->running->{done|failed->pending|dead} lifecycle.

metadata.land_summary: jobs schema hardening: live-job partial unique index (COALESCE prompt_ver) for idempotent enqueue (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), next_attempt_at backoff column, distinct 'dead' terminal + cli status surfaces dead-letters; docs/storage.md key formula/lifecycle pinned

With lode-u51 the gate now honors a threaded Settings (the eval path at cli.py:502 already passes one), but the interactive ask command still does not load/construct a user-configured Settings, so gate-tuning knobs like entailment_threshold remain inert from the interactive entry point. Harmless in v1 (threshold ships untuned) but the user-facing path can't honor config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cli.ask resolves/constructs a Settings and passes settings= into cited_answer.ask so a configured entailment_threshold (and other gate knobs) is honored from the interactive 'lode ask' path.
- A test proves a configured Settings reaches the gate via the CLI ask command (mirroring the offline ask-path test added in lode-u51).
- Depends on whatever CLI config-loading mechanism is decided (no config-file/env loader is wired into the ask command today).

Decide + implement the migration mechanism (see docs/decisions.md '$LODE_HOME migration'): (a) one-time move-if-present on startup (zero-touch, but the CLI relocates an irreplaceable DB — data-safety care: move lode.db, lode.db.lock, lancedb/ atomically, never clobber an existing ~/.lode, leave a marker) vs (b) document a manual move (release note / 'lode doctor' hint). title: Thread Settings into gate_cited_answer so entailment_threshold is honored on the ask path
description: cited_answer.gate_cited_answer calls gate.apply_gate(result.answer, bodies) without passing through ask()'s Settings, so the step-3 NLI entailment_threshold (and any future gate-tuning knob) falls back to the Settings() default regardless of a user's configured value. Harmless in v1 (the threshold ships untuned/conservative and is not meant to be tuned yet), but it means the knob is inert end-to-end. Fix: thread settings (and optionally an EntailmentScorer) from ask() -> gate_cited_answer -> apply_gate. Out of lode-1k3.4's declared file scope (gate/faithfulness/config only).

title: Eval harness: embed the dense-leg query with search_query prefix (asymmetric nomic)
description: lode.eval.harness._retrieve embeds the question via Embedder.embed_passages, which the production FastEmbedEmbedder prefixes with 'search_document: '. nomic-embed-text-v1.5 is asymmetric and expects 'search_query: ' for queries. Using the document prefix symmetrically biases the dense (cosine ANN) retrieval leg, softening recall@k quality when the harness is wired with the real embedder. The Embedder protocol (lode.embedding) currently exposes only embed_passages — fixing this means adding a query-embedding method to the seam (embedding.py), then using it in the harness query path. Lexical leg carries recall meanwhile, so impact is bounded.

title: lode ask: wire the dense (vector) retrieval leg
description: The 'lode ask' command (lode-y42.2) currently retrieves on the synchronous lexical leg alone; RRF scores a single-leg passage fine, so this is a valid subset. The dense (LanceDB cosine ANN) leg is deferred because it needs two pieces not yet landed: (1) the on-disk LanceDB location the capture-side indexing wiring establishes (lode-1f9 cache composition wires EmbeddingCacheBackend into the add path and owns where vectors live), and (2) a query-side embedding helper (the landed FastEmbedEmbedder.embed_passages uses the 'search_document:' prefix; nomic wants 'search_query:' for queries, so a query embed path must land). Once both exist, wire vector_search(store, conn, query_vector, k) into lode.cli._retrieve alongside the lexical leg. Acceptance: lode ask fuses lexical + dense legs via RRF over a populated store.

title: durable batch-handle persistence + resume-on-restart
description:
Persist submitted Claude Batch handles + their member jobs and resume on restart — re-poll the handle, ingest results, mark done; NEVER resubmit. This is the one thing reconciliation can't reconstruct: once a Batch is POSTed it's money in flight, and a reconcile scan would see "not yet enriched" and double-spend (docs/storage.md "The one thing reconciliation can't reconstruct: a submitted Batch"). It is the requirement that rules out an in-memory queue.

DEFERRED out of the core E2 embed pass — DECISION 2026-06-28: a batch_handle only exists once enrich-via-Batches (E7 / lode-npx.2) is built, so this is untestable until then and should land alongside it. The jobs.batch_handle column already exists in schema.sql; the resume hook is the worker's (i05.3) startup step. Blocked on lode-npx.2 (the Batches submit path that produces handles) and lode-i05.3 (the worker startup where resume runs).
design: On batch submit (E7): persist the batch_handle on the member enrich jobs and mark them in-flight ('running' with the handle set). On worker startup (i05.3), as a step alongside reconciliation: find jobs with a non-null batch_handle in a non-terminal state and re-poll the Batch — ingest completed results (write the enrichment, mark member jobs 'done'); leave a still-running handle for the next poll; NEVER re-submit. Because the in-flight rows are 'running' with a handle (not 'pending'), the reconciliation scan's "not yet enriched" gap query must skip them, so it can't double-spend.
acceptance_criteria: A persisted batch handle is re-polled and ingested on restart without resubmission; completed handles mark their member jobs 'done'; an in-flight handle survives restart and is not resubmitted; the reconciliation scan skips in-flight ('running' + handle) jobs so it cannot double-spend.

title: worker loop: claim -> run -> retry/backoff -> dead-letter
description: The single-owner worker that drains the durable jobs queue. Exposed as a Typer command `lode work` (worker model PINNED 2026-06-28): a ONE-SHOT DRAIN by default — acquire the advisory lock (i05.2), run the reconciliation scan (i05.4) on startup, then claim -> run ready jobs until none remain, release the lock, exit. One-shot is testable and serves the eval harness + scripted use now (Phase A has no long-running host process). A `--loop` / `--watch` flag runs the SAME loop polling on an interval as the long-running single owner. Once this lands, x6r.5 flips capture's skeleton inline-embed onto this queue.
design:
HANDLER REGISTRY: the worker dispatches on jobs.type via a registry. `embed` has a handler NOW (runs the existing chunk+embed+FTS path: lode.embedding.embed + lode.lexical). `enrich` and `refresh` handlers are registered later by E7 (npx) and the connectors step. A job whose type has NO registered handler is LEFT pending (never claimed, never dead-lettered) — so the enrich rows i05.1 enqueues per capture accumulate harmlessly until E7's handler arrives. The claim query therefore filters to types the worker can actually run.

CLAIM: select one ready, runnable job — status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now AND type IN (<registered handler types>) — ORDER BY priority (embed > enrich, docs/storage.md:274) then created. Atomically flip to 'running' with UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status='pending' and assert rowcount=1, so a stray second claimer can't double-take (belt-and-suspenders behind the single-owner lock).

RUN: invoke the type's handler.
  - ok -> status='done'.
  - transient error -> attempts += 1, last_error set, status back to 'pending' with next_attempt_at = now + exponential backoff (base/factor from lode.config); a restart mid-backoff does NOT retry early (the reason i05.6 added next_attempt_at). Mark 'failed' as the transient last-error state per i05.6's lifecycle.
  - max-attempts gate reached (config knob) -> status='dead' (i05.6's poison terminal), preserving attempts + last_error for the `lode status` read-out.

SINGLE OWNER: the whole loop runs under the i05.2 advisory lock; a second `lode work` refuses.

SCOPE FENCE: the worker loop + `lode work` command + the embed handler wiring. Does NOT remove capture's inline embed (that flip is x6r.5). Does NOT implement enrich/refresh handlers (E7 / connectors).
acceptance_criteria: A claimed embed job runs once and lands its passages/vectors/FTS; a transient failure retries with growing next_attempt_at backoff (not before next_attempt_at); a poison job reaches status='dead' with attempts + last_error recorded; 'lode work' drains all runnable jobs then exits and '--loop' keeps polling; an enrich job with no registered handler is left pending, never dead-lettered; the loop runs under the advisory lock (a second 'lode work' refuses).

metadata.land_summary: Async work queue worker (lode.worker) + 'lode work' Typer command: handler registry (embed only), atomic CAS claim, run_one state machine (done | failed+backoff | dead at max-attempts), durable next_attempt_at backoff, _reset_retryable + drain one-shot/--loop under the i05.2 WorkerLock (second invocation exits 1). Scope fence held: capture inline embed untouched, no enrich/refresh handlers (enrich left pending, never dead-lettered). Reviewer refactor: extracted _iso() for the schema-coupled ISO-8601 format.

title: reconciliation scan (startup + periodic)
description:
The self-healing net (docs/storage.md "Reconciliation scan on startup + periodically"). Scans head versions and re-enqueues any missing fresh derived work, so crashes, dropped jobs, the save/enqueue gap, and prompt_ver bumps all self-correct. Runs on worker startup (i05.3) and periodically in `--loop` mode. Idempotent by i05.6's key: re-enqueue is INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the live-job partial unique index, so running it repeatedly enqueues no duplicates.

Phase-A scope is the EMBED gap: a live head version (notes.head_version_id, excluding delete tombstones and purged notes) with no passages row for that version_id -> enqueue an embed job. The ENRICH gap (no fresh source='ai' enrichment for the head, or a prompt_ver bump made it stale -> re-enqueue the corpus) is a registered scan step filled by E7 — it needs the enrichment tables and prompt_ver semantics that don't exist yet. Mirror i05.3's handler-registry shape: scan steps for types that exist now run now; E7 appends the enrich step.
design:
EMBED GAP QUERY: head versions missing passages — e.g. notes joined to their head version, where the head op is not 'delete' and the note is not purged, and no passages row exists for head_version_id -> enqueue embed(head_version_id).

IDEMPOTENCY: the scan does NOT pre-check for an existing job; it relies entirely on i05.6's live-job partial unique index + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to dedupe. This is why i05.6 scopes the unique index to pending/running: a head whose embed is already 'done' but later goes stale (new head) enqueues against the NEW version_id, which has no live job, so it is correctly re-enqueued.

ONE ENQUEUE PATH: reuse the i05.1 Repository/jobs enqueue, not a second hand-rolled INSERT, so there is a single enqueue site.

SCOPE: embed-gap reconciliation + the periodic hook for `--loop`. Enrich-gap step is left as a seam for E7.
acceptance_criteria: A live head version with no fresh embed is re-enqueued by the scan; running the scan repeatedly enqueues no duplicate jobs (idempotent against i05.6's live-job unique index); a soft-deleted/purged head is not enqueued; enqueue reuses the single i05.1 enqueue path. (Enrich-gap reconciliation is a registered step filled by E7.)

Wired into 'lode work' before each drain pass (startup + every --loop tick). jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs gains a backward-compatible keyword-only types= param. Enrich-gap seam left open for E7 (register_step) with no dead code. Review: removed one redundant/misleading test; gates green (443 passed).

title: single-instance advisory lock
description:
Startup advisory lock (lockfile + PID, beside the DB under $LODE_HOME) so the async worker has a single owner (docs/storage.md "Single-instance = a startup advisory lock"). This lock is NOT a data-integrity guard — CAS + SQLite serialization cover correctness; it exists solely so two workers don't run duplicate / racing embed+enrich loops and double-spend Claude Batches (docs/storage.md:100-104). It is what lets the one-claimer SQLite queue (i05.3) stay correct with no distributed locking (docs/storage.md:280).

Behaviour: acquire on worker start (i05.3 `lode work`); if held by a LIVE pid, refuse to start and name the holding pid; release on clean exit. A lock left by a NO-LONGER-RUNNING pid is reclaimable (stale), not a permanent wedge — a crashed worker must not block the queue forever.
design:
Lockfile path under $LODE_HOME (lode.config paths). On acquire, write the current pid. On start:
  - file present AND pid alive  -> refuse: print "another lode worker is running (pid N)", non-zero exit.
  - file present AND pid dead   -> stale: reclaim (overwrite) and proceed.
  - file absent                 -> acquire.
Release = remove the file on clean exit (context manager / finally), so a normal exit frees it immediately.

SCOPE: the lock primitive + acquire/refuse/reclaim/release, with a direct test. Wiring it into the `lode work` loop is i05.3's job. Liveness check is best-effort (os.kill(pid, 0) / equivalent) — single-machine, single-user, so a pid-reuse false "alive" is acceptable; we are not building a distributed lock.
acceptance_criteria: A second acquisition refuses while the lock is held by a live pid and names that pid; the lock releases on clean exit; a lock left by a no-longer-running pid is reclaimed, not treated as held.

metadata.land_summary: Single-instance advisory lockfile primitive (lode.lock.WorkerLock): acquire writes PID beside the DB, refuse+name a live holder, reclaim a stale/corrupt lock, release on clean exit (context manager). Path derived from caller-supplied db_path (lode.config default_db_path), not re-derived; not wired into 'lode work' (that is i05.3). Reviewer reuse fix: 'lode config' now reads the lock path from lock.lock_path instead of re-deriving it.

title: jobs table + atomic enqueue in save txn
description: Durable jobs (type embed|enrich|refresh, target_version, prompt_ver?, status, attempts, last_error?, batch_handle?). Enqueue derive jobs in the SAME txn as the version write (single-file SQLite atomicity, docs/stack.md).
design:
ENQUEUE OWNERSHIP / ATOMICITY — DECISION PINNED 2026-06-28 (lode-i05 breakdown), supersedes the earlier "decide consciously" fork in this ticket.

OWNERSHIP: the Repository owns enqueue. It already owns the save+cache seam (irreplaceable version write, then cache index/evict); enqueueing a head version's derive jobs is the third thing that must happen on a head change, and jobs are operational/irreplaceable rows — so enqueue belongs at the Repository seam, NOT in the CLI and NOT buried in versions.py.

ATOMICITY / SEAM: refactor lode.versions.save (and delete/recover as the enqueue path needs) so the version-write runs inside a CALLER-MANAGED transaction instead of opening + committing its own `with conn:`. Repository.save then wraps the version-write AND the enqueue in ONE `with conn:`, so "write version row + enqueue its derive jobs" commits atomically (docs/storage.md:269 "enqueued in the same transaction as the save"). Job-type knowledge (jobs.DERIVE_JOB_TYPES) stays in jobs.py / the Repository — it never enters versions.py.

RETIRE the standalone path (kills the "two enqueue sites = hazard" the debate flagged):
  - jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs stops opening its own txn — it becomes a plain INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (against i05.6's live-job partial unique index) on the caller's conn, run inside Repository's transaction.
  - the direct caller in `lode add` (src/lode/cli.py:177) is removed; capture goes through Repository.save, now the SINGLE enqueue site.

BUILD ON i05.6: enqueue is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the live-job unique index, so a duplicate / reconcile re-enqueue is a no-op. Do not re-add the key here.

CONSTRAINTS: keep versions.save's CAS + no-op-dedup contract intact — only the transaction OWNERSHIP changes (save must not commit independently when Repository drives it). On a deduped no-op save, Repository enqueues NOTHING (same skip as the cache index). Editing versions.py is now permitted: the y42.1 lane fence that originally forbade it is gone. Record the pinned ownership/atomicity/layering choice in docs/storage.md (the async-queue section) so the decision lives in the design, not only in code.
acceptance_criteria: Writing a version and enqueuing its derive jobs commit in one transaction; an injected failure between the version-write and the enqueue (or in the enqueue) rolls back BOTH — no version without its jobs, no jobs without the version. A deduped no-op save enqueues nothing. lode add no longer calls jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs directly; Repository.save is the sole enqueue site. The pinned ownership/atomicity choice is recorded in docs/storage.md.

metadata.land_summary: Atomic save+enqueue: Repository.save wraps versions._save_core (CAS write, no own txn) + jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs (plain ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert) in one 'with conn:' so version-write + derive-job enqueue commit/rollback together; dedup no-op enqueues nothing; lode add + eval harness route through Repository.save as the sole enqueue site (cli no longer calls jobs directly); ownership/atomicity/layering pinned in docs/storage.md

title: E2 — Async work queue & single-owner
description: Durable jobs table per docs/storage.md: atomic enqueue in the same txn as save (single-file SQLite); single-instance advisory lock (lockfile/PID); worker loop claim->run->backoff-retry->dead-letter; reconciliation scan (startup+periodic) re-enqueues head versions missing fresh embed/enrich, idempotent by key; durable batch-handle persistence + resume-on-restart (the one thing reconcile cannot reconstruct without double-spend).
acceptance_criteria: All E2 tasks closed: derive jobs enqueue atomically with the save, a single owner runs the claim/retry/dead-letter loop, the reconciliation scan self-heals idempotently, and batch handles resume without double-spend.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-06-28, E1->E2 handoff): landed jobs table + enqueue do NOT support the E2 ACs as written.
1. jobs table has NO idempotency key (INTEGER PK + non-unique idx_jobs_status only); enqueue_derive_jobs plain-INSERTs, so double-enqueue / reconcile re-enqueue = duplicate pending rows. 'Idempotent by key' (E2 AC, docs/storage.md:264) has nothing to be idempotent against.
2. Key formula in docs/storage.md:264 (version_id | version_id+prompt_ver) OMITS type, so embed+enrich for one version collide. Real key is (type,target_version[,prompt_ver]); prompt_ver is NULL on embed rows and SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE, so naive UNIQUE won't dedupe embed. Must coalesce/partial-key.
3. 'Atomic enqueue in same txn as save' (docs/storage.md:269) is ALREADY VIOLATED: jobs.py enqueues in a SEPARATE txn (y42.1 lane fence forbade editing versions.py). E2.1 is a refactor+migration: fold enqueue into versions.save txn AND retire standalone enqueue_derive_jobs + its CLI caller. Two enqueue sites = hazard.
4. versions.save() has no seam for same-txn enqueue (opens+commits own 'with conn:'). Folding in forces a layering decision: push job-type knowledge into versions.py (the coupling jobs.py avoided) vs restructure save to expose its open txn. Decide consciously; record in docs/storage.md.
5. Enqueue ownership unsettled across 3 layers: CLI calls jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs; Repository.save indexes cache but never enqueues; versions.save knows nothing of jobs. Collides with E2 'single owner'. Pin one home, reconcile with the Repository irreplaceable-vs-cache seam.
6. jobs schema lacks worker-loop columns: status CHECK is pending/running/done/failed (no dead-letter terminal distinct from transient failed); no next_attempt_at/not-before for durable backoff (restart mid-backoff retries immediately). E2.3 backoff+dead-letter not implementable without schema change or a pinned max-attempts policy.
RESOLUTION: leading schema-hardening ticket (idempotency key, next_attempt_at, dead-letter terminal) blocks the jobs-table/enqueue work; record the enqueue-ownership/layering decision in docs/storage.md.
BREAKDOWN PINNED 2026-06-28 (4 decisions resolved with bildzeitung):
1. Worker model: one-shot 'lode work' drain by default + '--loop' polling mode (no daemon/TUI host in Phase A); not an in-process thread. -> i05.3.
2. Batch resume (i05.5) DEFERRED to land with E7: a batch_handle only exists once enrich-via-Batches (npx.2) is built, so it is untestable now. i05.5 dep-linked to npx.2 + i05.3.
3. Enqueue seam: Repository OWNS enqueue; refactor versions.save to run inside a caller-managed txn so Repository.save commits version-write + enqueue atomically; retire jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs's standalone txn and the lode-add caller (one enqueue site). -> i05.1.
