title: Repository.recover() feeds cache.index() an unredacted body (redact-before-index gap)
description:
lode-n60 wired redact_before_index() into Repository.save() (the body handed to CacheBackend.index()) and into embedding.embed() (the vector leg's own re-read of versions.body). Repository.recover() has the identical shape — it reads the target version's raw body via self._body(target_version) and hands it straight to self.cache.index(note_id, result.version_id, body) with no redaction — so recovering a version whose body matches a redact_before_index_patterns seed would push the raw secret into the FTS leg (LexicalCacheBackend.index() uses the body param verbatim). embed()'s own internal redaction protects the vector leg regardless of caller, so only the FTS/lexical leg is actually exposed today. recover() is not yet CLI-wired (no 'lode recover' command exists), so this is currently latent, not reachable in production — but should be fixed before any CLI wiring lands.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. repo.save("note-1", "key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE done")
2. repo.delete("note-1", parent=<that version>)
3. repo.recover("note-1", target_version=<the secret-bearing version>)
4. LexicalIndex(conn).search("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", k=5) returns a hit — the secret is keyword-findable again post-recover.

## Acceptance Criteria
Repository.recover() applies lode.redact.redact_before_index() to the body before calling self.cache.index(), same pattern as save() (lode-n60). recover() gains a settings: Settings | None = None parameter (it currently has none) so the patterns can be resolved. A regression test proves a recovered secret-bearing version is not keyword-findable via LexicalIndex.search().

metadata.land_summary: Wire redact_before_index() into Repository.recover()'s cache seam: recover() gains settings param; recovered head's raw body (_body) is redacted before cache.index() so a recovered secret-bearing version is not FTS-findable; versions.body stays raw; +2 regression tests. Technical review: no bug/simplify changes — faithful mirror of lode-n60 save() path.

title: Batch-submit enrich jobs don't stamp claimed_at before batch_handle persist (early-reclaim risk)
description:
Context: surfaced during lode-aor's technical review (crash-recovery for stuck 'running' jobs).

lode-aor added _reclaim_stale_running(), which reclaims any job in status='running'
with batch_handle IS NULL past a staleness timeout, on the assumption that claimed_at
is stamped on every path that flips a job to 'running' (true for _claim_one).

_batch_submit_enrich (worker.py, ~L526-530) flips enrich jobs to 'running' WITHOUT
stamping claimed_at. If a crash lands in the narrow window between
submit_enrich_batch's batches.create() returning and the batch_handle persist
(enrich.py:465-474), the row is left running + batch_handle NULL + claimed_at NULL.
_reclaim_stale_running treats claimed_at IS NULL as immediately stale, so it will
reclaim (and eventually resubmit) that job -- risking a duplicate Batches API
submission if the original batch_handle write was actually about to succeed.

This is pre-existing batch-path non-atomicity, not introduced by lode-aor. lode-aor's
new behavior is still a net improvement (trades "stuck forever + orphaned batch" for
"eventual resubmit"), so it was not blocking and did not need to land with a fix.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Kick off a bulk enrich batch submission (_batch_submit_enrich).
2. Kill the process between batches.create() returning in submit_enrich_batch and the
   batch_handle UPDATE persisting (enrich.py:465-474).
3. Restart and let drain() run past the staleness timeout.
4. Observe: the row (running, batch_handle NULL, claimed_at NULL) is reclaimed and
   resubmitted even though the original batch may have gone through -- possible
   duplicate Batches API spend.

## Acceptance Criteria
Either (a) stamp claimed_at when _batch_submit_enrich flips a job to 'running' (so it
gets a real staleness window instead of being treated as immediately stale), or (b)
make the batch_handle persist atomic/two-phase with the running-flip, so this window
cannot exist. Scope belongs with the batch path (lode-i05.5's owner), not with
lode-aor's staleness-reclaim mechanism.

metadata.land_summary: Stamp claimed_at in _batch_submit_enrich's pre-claim CAS (worker.py) so a crash between batches.create() and the batch_handle persist (enrich.py) leaves batch-path rows a real 900s staleness window instead of being treated as immediately stale by _reclaim_stale_running (lode-aor). +2 regression tests. Gates green: 601 passed/4 skipped.

title: Reclaim stuck 'running' jobs after a crash (no TTL/timeout reclaim exists)
description:
Context: found while designing the fix for lode-npx.2's double-enrichment bug.

worker.py's claim/run state machine has no mechanism to reclaim a job left in
status='running' by a crash. _reset_retryable (worker.py) only resets
status='failed' jobs whose next_attempt_at is due back to 'pending' -- it never
touches 'running' rows. _claim_one only ever selects status='pending'. So a
worker (or, once lode-npx.2's fix lands, the CLI's inline immediate-enrich
claim) that crashes or is killed between claiming a job (UPDATE ... SET
status='running') and completing it leaves that row permanently stuck: no
reconciliation step, no gap query, and no claim query will ever pick it up
again.

This is NOT specific to enrich -- it applies identically to embed jobs claimed
by the normal `lode work` worker loop. worker.py's own module docstring
half-acknowledges this ("Regular embed jobs left running by a crash are
covered by the embed-gap reconciliation query if the embed result is also
missing") but that claim doesn't hold: reconcile.py's embed_gap / enrich_gap
queries both exclude any job with status != 'dead' (which includes 'running')
from being treated as a gap, so a genuinely stuck 'running' row is invisible
to reconciliation too.

Pre-existing gap, not introduced by any one ticket -- surfacing it now because
lode-npx.2's fix (CLI opportunistically claims+runs the enrich job it just
enqueued, same primitives as the worker) adds a new trigger for it: a crash or
Ctrl-C during `lode add` mid-Haiku-call, in addition to the existing
worker-crash trigger.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run \`lode work\` (or, after lode-npx.2 lands, \`lode add\`) and kill the
   process (SIGKILL) after it flips a job row to status='running' but before
   the handler completes.
2. Run \`lode work\` again (fresh process).
3. Observe: the killed job's row stays status='running' forever -- it is never
   re-claimed, never appears in \`lode jobs\` as a gap, and reconcile's
   embed_gap/enrich_gap steps do not re-enqueue it (both queries treat any
   status != 'dead' row, including 'running', as \"not a gap\").
design: Root cause: no signal exists for 'how long has this job been running', so nothing can distinguish a legitimately in-flight job from one abandoned by a crash. _claim_one only selects status='pending'; reconcile's embed_gap/enrich_gap queries exclude any status != 'dead' (including 'running'). Fix: add jobs.claimed_at (ISO-8601 UTC, set by _claim_one's claim UPDATE); a new lode.worker._reclaim_stale_running(conn, settings), run at the top of every drain() pass before _reset_retryable, selects status='running' AND batch_handle IS NULL AND (claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at <= now - settings.stale_running_timeout_s new Settings knob, default 900s) and puts each through the identical attempts/backoff/dead-letter accounting run_one uses for a transient handler failure (reuse, no parallel retry policy). Batch-backed enrich jobs are excluded via batch_handle IS NOT NULL (lode-i05.5 owns their long-lived running + resume-on-restart semantics). Once reclaimed to dead or pending, reconcile's existing gap queries see the job correctly with no changes of their own.
acceptance_criteria: A job stuck in status='running' past some staleness threshold (e.g. no update to the row for N minutes, or a dead process' pid) is detected and reclaimed -- either reset to 'pending' for retry, or dead-lettered if attempts are exhausted -- without manual DB surgery. Applies uniformly to embed, enrich, and refresh job types. Batches-backed enrich jobs (batch_handle set) are explicitly excluded (lode-i05.5 already owns their long-lived 'running' + resume-on-restart semantics).
notes: Reviewer (technical review pass) surfaced a related but out-of-scope gap: _batch_submit_enrich flips enrich jobs to 'running' without stamping claimed_at before the batch_handle persist completes, so a crash in that window could trigger an early reclaim -> possible duplicate batch resubmission. Filed as lode-uhu (belongs to the batch path / lode-i05.5's owner, not this ticket's staleness-reclaim scope).

metadata.land_summary: Reclaim stuck status='running' jobs after a crash: adds jobs.claimed_at (schema+migration), Settings.stale_running_timeout_s (900s), and worker._reclaim_stale_running run atop every drain() pass; reuses run_one's attempts/backoff/dead-letter accounting, excludes batch-backed enrich jobs. Review verified correctness + hoisted a loop-invariant. 12 tests, all gates green.
